note: NHES-ECPP 2019 public-use has real hours per arrangement (CAREHOURX, CPHRS, RCHRS, NCHRS) for 4132 children, and gives a part-time share at the build's own 20 hrs/week cut: 0.311 NE, 0.314 S, 0.270 MW, 0.330 W. feeds: step 6 -- blends the two paid-centre price bands into one Center-Based row
candidate: DOL Women's Bureau National Database of Childcare Prices (NDCP), 2008-2022
note: NDCP gives median and 75th-percentile prices by county, provider type (center / family) and age, and is fetchable from Bouchet (www.dol.gov is 403 from Windows, 200 there). BUT every price is a FULL-TIME WEEKLY price and there is NO part-time series, so the grid's 10 hrs/week point has no NDCP price. Worse for a state build, "full-time" is each state's own definition and is not a fixed number of hours: ME reports 21-30 hrs most frequent, IN 35, MI 45, NJ 51.7, and several states let each provider decide. Using NDCP across states would import variation in the DEFINITION of full-time as if it were variation in price. Hourly-reporting states are converted at x40 hrs/week, which matches the simulator's full-time point only by coincidence. Technical report in raw/documentation/.
